newsitem.title: INDIA: Rescuers seek 20 missing after India ship sinks.
newsitem.headline: Rescuers seek 20 missing after India ship sinks.

text.p: Rescue teams hunted for 20 crewmen missing after a cargo vessel sank off India's west coast on Thursday killing four people, hours before another ship went down in a river near the eastern city of Calcutta.
"We're still searching for 20 of the 33-member crew missing after the vessel sank in bad weather this morning," a defence spokesman told Reuters in Bombay.
Hospital staff said four of the 13 rescued had died soon after being taken to hospital.
The ship, the M.V. Arcadia Pride, had a deadweight of 13,672 tonnes and was loaded with sulphur, officials said. It sank at anchorage seven nautical miles off Bombay, around 9 a.m. (0330 GMT).
India's navy and coastguard used five helicopters and two ships in the search, the spokesman said. "The choppers are flying regular sorties over the area where the ship went down."
Survivors said the ship had waited for three days for a berth in the harbour. In a sudden squall early on Thursday, the anchor started dragging and had to be raised.
"We were replacing it again when the ship got hit by a swell and the loose cargo shifted," said one of the survivors. "Then the ship capsized, immediately within the next five minutes."
"The waves were around 30 feet high," added C.G. Balakrishnan, 50, a motorman on the vessel. "Suddenly, around 8.30 a.m., it started shaking.

"Water started filling the cabin," Balakrishnan told Reuters. "Through the porthole I could see only water. I started running up the stairs, but the ladder was almost vertical. I desperately climbed it, and was thrown off the ship.
"Then I managed to find a buoy, and clung on, till I was finally rescued by a naval helicopter."
Officials at Arcadia Shipping Pvt. Ltd, which owned the vessel, said they were awaiting details of the rescue operations.
"The ship was carrying bulk cargo from the United Arab Emirates," said a spokesman. "We are waiting for details."
In another incident near the eastern city of Calcutta, police said all 20 crew were rescued after the Panama-flag M.V. Green Opal sank in the Hooghly river after a collision with a barge.
"All the 20 crew members were rescued," senior police official K.K. Kalia told Reuters. He said the ship, on its way to Keelong near Singapore, sank 40 km (25 miles) from Calcutta.
Kalia said two of the crew members were Korean and the rest Filipino.

Port officials said there was little hope of recovering the 7,000 tonnes of steel coils and billets the vessel was carrying. Earlier, the Press Trust of India (PTI) reported the cargo was 70,000 tonnes of steel coils and billets.
PTI quoted port officials as saying they were planning to lift the damaged ship from the water. A senior port official told Reuters that traffic would not be disrupted.
"With careful manoeuvring it will be possible to maintain shipping movement," the offical said. The shipping channel had not been blocked, he added.
